notes: Data SOURCE for the lifecycle-vs-players comparison on public/site/agentic-governance-lifecycle.html.

Narrative player-by-category prose is canonically owned by public/site/learn/articles/players-in-ai-governance.html (the four camps) and public/site/analyst-briefing/competitive-landscape.html (the altitude argument). This registry maps named players onto lifecycle STAGES — the cut neither narrative page makes — and links back to them rather than re-describing.
Every public_positioning claim is sourced from the cited source_url (the vendor's own public site). Factual only.
covers_stage_ids[] is capped at three per the schema: external players cover a slice; KYE (kye_self) spans all ten — that contrast is the visual.

players.name: Datadog
players.public_positioning: Datadog LLM Observability monitors, troubleshoots and evaluates LLM applications in production — tracing, quality and performance metrics for model and agent behaviour.

players.name: Arize AI
players.public_positioning: Arize positions itself as an AI observability and LLM evaluation platform for tracing, evaluating and troubleshooting agents and model performance in production.

players.name: Robust Intelligence (Cisco AI Defense)
players.public_positioning: Cisco AI Defense (incorporating Robust Intelligence) publicly describes automated AI validation and runtime safety for models and applications — algorithmic red-teaming and guardrails.

players.name: Credo AI
players.public_positioning: Credo AI publicly positions an AI governance platform for use-case registration, policy management and regulatory framework mapping (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF).

players.name: OneTrust
players.public_positioning: OneTrust AI Governance publicly offers an AI inventory, risk assessment and policy management workflow for cataloguing and governing AI systems against regulatory requirements.

players.name: Cerbos
players.public_positioning: Cerbos publicly describes a stateless, decoupled authorization (PDP) layer that evaluates policy-as-code to allow or deny actions on resources, including for AI agents.

players.name: Temporal
players.public_positioning: Temporal publicly offers a durable execution platform that orchestrates and enforces reliable, recoverable workflow state transitions — the enforcement layer KYE decides admissibility for.

players.name: Lakera
players.public_positioning: Lakera Guard publicly screens prompts and agent inputs for injection, jailbreak and data-leak risk — an input-admissibility signal that feeds, but does not replace, an authority decision.
